title: Shadow pin deferral and rollforward runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook documents an operational strategy we call 'shadow pin deferral'—a lightweight way to defer hard region pin enforcement while maintaining auditable evidence and safe rollforward/rollback paths. It is intended for on-call operators, SREs, and Solutions Engineers who run pin migrations or respond to pin-related incidents.

Context / motivation (short):
- Hard pin enforcement can break customers during migrations, legal clarifications, or cloud-region outages.
- A shadow-deferral mode lets traffic continue to be served while we capture per-request evidence and maintain a path to later enforce (rollforward) or revert (rollback) according to legal or customer-facing decisions.
- This doc sketches concrete operator steps, telemetry signals, and decision heuristics to use during a shadow-deferral window.

Key concepts (defs):
- Shadow pin: a parallel evaluation that records where a request WOULD have been routed/enforced if a hard-pin was active, without preventing the current path.
- Deferral window: configurable period (e.g., 7–30 days) where customers are allowed to continue without strict enforcement while evidence is gathered.
- Rollforward: the action of turning a shadow pin into an active (hard) pin after validation.
- Rollback: canceling the shadow and leaving routing as-is permanently.

High-level flow:
1) Customer or legal triggers pin change request (sales/prod tile).
2) Create shadow-pin entry in system (metadata + TTL = deferral window).
3) Enable shadowing on routing layer — requests are routed normally but the routing engine writes a shadow record (region, model variant, reason, acceptance flags) to the audit store.
4) Run telemetry and QA during deferral window (synthetic and live samples).
5a) If audit + QA pass -> rollforward (enable hard pin, update contracts, notify customer).
5b) If issues found -> rollback (remove shadow, optionally add mitigations or schedule migration).

Operator checklist (quick):
- Before enabling shadow: has customer signed exception? (see Confluence page). Attach JIRA key to shadow entry.
- Create shadow entry: run ./ops/create_shadow_pin --tenant <TENANT_ID> --region eu-west-1 --ttl-days 14 --reason "legal-review" --jira JIRA-9482
- Confirm shadow propagation: check /internal-api/shadow-status/<TENANT> returns active.
- Turn on request-level sampling: set sample rate = 100% for first 6 hours, then 5–10% for remainder. Use trace tag shadow_pin=true.

Telemetry signals to watch (early-warning):
- Shadow mismatch rate: proportion of requests where shadow target != served region. Spike >2% for >1h -> investigate.
- Latency delta: requests where served latency increased >20ms vs non-shadow baseline.
- KV-cache hit erosion: frequent cache misses when region differs.
- Exported PII redaction flags: any request that triggers redaction heuristics when shadow region would have stored different retention.
- Customer error rate: 4xx/5xx drift during sampling window.

Example PromQL-ish checks (SRE copy/paste):
- shadow_mismatch_ratio = sum(shadow_mismatch_total{tenant=~"$TENANT"}) / sum(shadow_sampled_total{tenant=~"$TENANT"})
- shadow_avg_latency_delta_ms = avg_over_time((latency_served_ms - latency_shadow_ms)[1h])

QA & acceptance criteria (minimal):
- Audit evidence completeness: >98% of sampled requests contain a shadow record with region and model-version fields.
- No regression in client-observed success rate > 0.5% absolute.
- No unresolved legal flags (KYC/PII) in sample set.
- Operator sign-off from SRE + Solutions Eng.

Rollforward steps (safe path):
1) Schedule 30-minute maintenance window (optional) and notify customer (if required by contract).
2) Re-run snapshot QA (last 24h). Attach QA report to JIRA.
3) Run ./ops/commit_pin --tenant <TENANT> --region <REGION> --shadow-id <ID> --commit-message "rollforward after QA"
4) Verify policy propagation to runtime (check /internal-api/pin-status).
5) Reduce shadow sampling flags and mark shadow entry as 'committed' in audit store.
6) Post-rollforward telemetry: monitor mismatch rate -> should go to 0 quickly.
7) Update billing/tagging and legal evidence package.

Rollback steps (when to choose):
- Significant mismatch (>5%) that cannot be explained by configuration.
- Customer experiments show broken UX/regressions.
- Legal team revokes consent or evidence is insufficient.
Steps:
1) Mark shadow as 'revoked' in audit store: ./ops/revoke_shadow --id <ID> --reason "QA fail"
2) Revert any temporary routing rules and ensure no partial enforcement remains.
3) Open follow-up ticket for migration plan or extended remediation.
4) Inform customer and CS.

Audit evidence packaging (what we attach to contracts):
- Sampled request CSV (timestamp, request_id, served_region, shadow_region, model_version, redact_flags)
- QA runbook notes and who signed off
- Telemetry graphs (mismatch ratio, latency delta, errors)
- Operator command logs for create/commit/revoke actions

Edge cases & gotchas (notes to ops):
- Multi-region tenants: shadow target may differ per customer region preference—ensure the shadow entry includes per-account mapping.
- Data-store sticky sessions: ephemeral session pins may continue to route to legacy region. Add session-id correlation in evidence.
- Cache warmup: early latency spikes are expected; use 6–12h warmup before judging latency.
- Partial model compatibility: if shadow region has a quantized variant, note model-variant in evidence so we can reason about quality diffs.

Testing harness (dev steps):
- Local: ./scripts/fake_shadow_traffic --tenant $T --qps 20 --duration 15m --region eu-west-1 --sample 100
- Staging: run leak test with 1% of production buckets for 48h. Check the shadow_mismatch_ratio and error budgets.

Runbook snippets (operator copy/paste):
- create: ./ops/create_shadow_pin --tenant T123 --region eu-west-1 --ttl-days 14 --reason "legal-review" --jira JIRA-9482
- status: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api/redwood/shadow-status/T123
- revoke: ./ops/revoke_shadow --id SHADOW-2025-11 --reason "QA fail"

Open questions / TODOs (work items):
- [ ] auto-escalation threshold: should mismatch ratio >3% auto-blast to #residency-alerts? (Priya to prototype)
- [ ] evidence retention policy: where and how long to keep sampled payloads (security review blocked) (Legal: Ethan)
- [ ] UX for customers to opt-in to deferral vs. immediate enforcement (Product/CS design required)

References and related docs:
- Confluence: Shadow Pin Spec (linked above)
- Oncall playbooks: region-pin-failure-playbook (see SRE drive)
- GitHub ops tooling: ops-scripts repo PR #213

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally prescriptive with operator commands so oncall can follow quickly. Look for missing checks and add any tenant-specific exceptions.
- I intentionally kept the deferral window examples conservative (14 days) — legal may prefer longer for audits.
